text.title: Deal with EU not dependent on tuition fees agreement, Miliband says
text.body_text: - Published A deal agreed between the UK and the European Union on Friday will come into force regardless of whether the two sides can negotiate a separate tuition fees agreement, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has told the BBC.…
text.summary: Brussels sources had previously suggested the bloc might not apply the wider deal until fees were lowered for EU students in Britain.

text.body_text: A tech titan is brought down by the oldest trick in the book: a honeytrap. text.summary: Dominic West and Sienna Miller’s divorce battle has made for a rollicking potboiler in prestige drama clothing. As it approaches its explosive finale, expect the show to become a TV fixture A tech titan is brought down by the oldest trick in the book: a honeytrap. In the week that Nvidia’s Jensen Huang , co-founder of the world’s most valuable chip company, worth a whopping $4tn (£3tn), resigned over revelations that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, divorce drama War could hardly feel more timely. That’s also how the HBO/Sky legal thriller begins. Billionaire social media mogul Morgan Henderson (Dominic West in textbook posh rotter mode) has a hotel tryst with an alluring stranger after an awards show. She turns out to be in cahoots with his wife, Hollywood star Carla Duval (played with icy glamour by Sienna Miller), to prove her husband’s infidelity. Mission most definitely accomplished. audio.title: Are your body clocks off? Meet ‘circadian depression’
audio.description: What if depression is sometimes linked to your body’s internal sense of time? That’s what researchers from the University of Sydney’s Brain and Mind Centre wanted to know. In a new study, they surveyed patients with depression whose symptoms may reflect problems with their circadian rhythms – like their sleep schedule, how tired they feel in the morning and whether they’re a night owl. They found that about 1 in 4 qualified for what might be termed a circadian subtype of depression. And while there’s still a lot of research to be done, this could open up new pathways for mental health treatment. NPR health correspondent Will Stone walks us through the study and its implications. audio.title: How WW2 pushed the world to the brink
audio.description: In the 1930s, how did a world that many considered civilised collapse into barbarity? And how did ordinary people's hopes and fears across the globe help to drive the world towards catastrophe? Drawing on a trove of wartime letters and reports on morale from across international archives, historian Jonathan Fennell offers a remarkable new perspective on the Second World War. In today's episode, he explains to Elinor Evans why we should look beyond the usual 1939 to '45 narrative, and towards a much more global picture. ----- GO BEYOND THE PODCAST Hear more from Jonathan Fennell answering listener questions on the North African campaign in the Second World War here: https://bit.ly/4hlPEqP ----- GET MORE WITH MEMBERSHIP Become a HistoryExtra podcast member and unlock access to The Full Story podcast, plus enjoy ad-free listening, early access to other podcast episodes, and a member-exclusive newsletter.
